method: Port of FEATUREFINDER/FeatureFinderAlgorithmPickedHelperStructs.h and .cpp. The 14 START_SECTIONs of the class test are transcribed with their literals and comparison macros. An oracle driver outside this repository replays the same inputs plus 13 boundary cases against the product-SDK libOpenMS; its output is retained here and replayed row for row with floats compared bit for bit.
evidence_tier: tier 1 (executed differential: product-SDK libOpenMS oracle, 164 rows replayed bit for bit) for every computational member: getConvexhull, updateMaximum, getAvgMZ, MassTrace::isValid, MassTraces::isValid, getPeakCount, getTheoreticalmaxPosition, updateBaseline, getRTBounds, computeIntensityProfile, Seed::operator<, IsotopePattern(Size) and TheoreticalIsotopePattern::size, where the getConvexhull rows hold no signed-zero m/z (a known difference, see native_boundaries); tier 3 (transcribed class-test literals and comparison macros, all 14 sections); tier 4 (the accessors MassTraces::reserve, clear, get/get_mut, last/last_mut, iter/iter_mut, as_slice, is_empty and the IntoIterator impls, and PatternPeak::index; the native ceilings, the NaN-merge error and default values)

fixtures.kind: oracle-generated (tier 1 executed differential, Linux x86_64 Release)
fixtures.role: ../oracle/ffap-complete-min6 drivers/baseline_driver.cpp, node/run_baseline.sh: what MassTraces::updateBaseline leaves in baseline for 18 f32 intensity patterns in five peak layouts, twice each and identical - the pattern, the layout and the resulting f64 as an IEEE-754 bit pattern; written by extract/make_baseline_fixture.py. It pins the cvtss2sd promotion of update_baseline with executed bits, where the macOS-arm64 oracle above records only is_nan() for the one NaN case it has.

class_test_review.literal_extraction: All literals are transcribed verbatim, including the f32 intensity literals with digits beyond f32 precision; the file allows clippy::excessive_precision for that reason. The source test mutates shared state between sections: mt1 is copied into mt after its updateMaximum section, mt2 is pushed after the getPeakCount section, and three border peaks are added to mt[1] before computeIntensityProfile. Each Rust test rebuilds that state in the same order.
class_test_review.comparison: TEST_EQUAL is exact equality after converting the expected value to the actual value's type (ClassTest.h:224-245). TEST_REAL_SIMILAR is isRealSimilar with absdiff_max_allowed 1e-5 and ratio_max_allowed 1 + 1e-5 (ClassTest.cpp:35-38 and 364-470), transcribed in f64; the source evaluates in long double, and the transcribed cases are far from both limits. TEST_EXCEPTION(Exception::Precondition, ...) becomes Err(Error::InvalidValue(_)).

oracle.sdk: product-sdk, Debug build of core 4fdec46b205459b92e7d3b9e56df5d8e912d5c85, AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101, C++23
oracle.revision_equivalence: 4fdec46 is an ancestor of bc9cc12; git diff --stat 4fdec46 bc9cc12 is empty for the helper-struct header and implementation, ConvexHull2D.h/.cpp, Peak1D.h/.cpp, DBoundingBox.h, DIntervalBase.h and DPosition.h.
oracle.environment: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=<scratch>/home OPENMS_HOME_PATH=<scratch>/home OPENMS_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=ON OPENMS_DATA_PATH=product-sdk/share/OpenMS/4.0.0, per-run scratch working directory
oracle.reproduction: Two runs from separate scratch directories produced byte-identical output.
oracle.comparison: Exact: every row string equal, so every f64 matches bit for bit. The Rust replay was checked on the Linux x86-64 build node (IBMI kim), with its current stable toolchain and with 1.85.0, with default and with no default features, against the macOS arm64 oracle output. This bitwise contract is deliberately stricter than the early-bundle plan, which asserts bit equality only on macOS arm64 against the same-platform oracle and 1e-9 relative elsewhere. The recorded members use only basic arithmetic, comparisons and fabs, so no libm result enters. The one expression a compiler may contract, getAvgMZ's sum += mz * intensity, gives the same bits contracted and uncontracted for the recorded mt_avg and boundary inexact cases (checked with Python math.fma; the products of mt1 are exact), so the retained rows do not depend on whether the Debug oracle contracts. Regenerating the oracle from a Release or FMA-contracting build, or adding getAvgMZ cases, requires re-measuring before the bitwise assertion is kept.

oracle_reference_build.comparison: Exact: the port rebuilds all 90 configurations and compares f64 bit patterns (update_baseline_promotion_is_the_reference_builds_bits). A plain f64::from was measured to give the same bits on macOS arm64 for every pattern, so the fixture pins the value and not the choice of instruction; math::x86_64::widen is kept because Rust does not guarantee a NaN payload across a float cast.

source_anchors.operation: IsotopePattern(Size): peak(size, -1), four zero vectors, default-initialised theoretical_pattern
getConvexhull: addPoints over (RT, m/z) into a std::map keyed by RT
updateMaximum: strict float >, first maximum wins; empty trace returns early
getAvgMZ: double sums of mz*float and float, then quotient
MassTraces::isValid: fewer than 2 traces false; fabs(seed_mz - avg) <= tolerance
getTheoreticalmaxPosition: Precondition on empty; strict > keeps the first maximum
updateBaseline: 0 when empty; first peak seeds, strict < replaces; untouched when no trace has peaks
getRTBounds: Precondition on empty; starts at (DBL_MAX, -DBL_MAX)
computeIntensityProfile: first trace copied unchecked, later traces merged by a single std::list walk with exact RT equality; double += float

std::sort(seeds.rbegin(), seeds.rend()) orders the seeds by descending intensity through Seed::operator<, the first of its two uses; std::sort is not stable, so equal intensities have no defined order
updateBaseline, baseline scaled by 0.75, updateMaximum on traces[max_trace]
debug mode writes debug/abort_reasons.featureXML by walking abort_reasons_ in ascending Seed::operator< order, with RT, m/z and intensity taken at the key seed's position and unique id = index
input map sorted before run_; afterwards only float data arrays change, never peak m/z or intensity (supports copied TracePeak values)
abort_ stores abort_reasons_[seed] = reason in debug mode; seeds of equal intensity are one key, so the first seed stored keeps its position and takes the last reason
pattern.peak compared against -2 (removed) and -1 (missing); no other negative value is assigned
duplicate FeatureFinderDefs struct (IndexPair, IndexSet, ChargedIndexSet, Flag, NoSuccessor); unused in source/FEATUREFINDER
std::map<Seed, std::string> abort_reasons_ is ordered by Seed::operator<, the second of its two uses
IsotopeCluster::IndexSet and ChargedIndexSet typedefs for the legacy Fitter1D family, the other route to IsotopeCluster.h

native_boundaries: MassTrace peaks are (spectrum index, peak index) plus copied rt f64, mz f64 and intensity f32; max_peak is Option<TracePeak>, and pointer identity becomes index equality

Seed exposes is_less_intense_than instead of PartialOrd, because an intensity-only order would contradict the structural PartialEq. The source's operator< orders std::sort of the seeds and keys the debug-mode abort_reasons_ map; a caller that reproduces debug/abort_reasons.featureXML must key by is_less_intense_than, so that seeds of equal intensity collapse into one entry with the first seed's position and the last reason
IsotopePattern::peak is a PatternPeak enum (NotFound = -1, Removed = -2, Found(index)); the source assigns no other negative value

IsotopePattern::new refuses more than 100,000 isotopes; MassTraces::reserve refuses a capacity above 100,000 traces and maps allocation failure to Error::InvalidValue, leaving the collection unchanged
MassTraces::intensity_profile refuses more than 1,000,000 total peaks or more than 100,000,000 worst-case merge steps before allocating; an index-linked list reproduces the std::list insertion cost

MassTraces::intensity_profile returns Error::InvalidValue where the source loop never terminates (a NaN retention time meeting a profile entry), and an empty profile where the source dereferences begin() of an empty vector
MassTrace::convex_hull refuses non-finite coordinates and more than 1,000,000 peaks; the source accepts infinities as map keys

Known difference: MassTrace::convex_hull merges the m/z range of one retention time through kernel ConvexHull2D::add_points with f64::min and f64::max, and Rust leaves their sign for -0.0 against +0.0 unspecified, while the source keeps the first value (DBoundingBox<1>::encloses and strict < and > in ConvexHull2D::addPoint). An independent review fuzz against product-SDK libOpenMS (not retained) found 2 differing hull rows on Linux x86-64 and 1 on macOS arm64 in a hand-built signed-zero case. m/z is positive on the FeatureFinderCentroided path and the retained rows hold no signed zero; the fix belongs in the kernel
get, get_mut, last and last_mut return Option; Index and IndexMut panic on out-of-range indices like slices
Scalars the source leaves uninitialised (max_rt, theoretical_int, baseline, TheoreticalIsotopePattern scalars) start at zero

MassTrace::avg_mz, MassTraces::update_baseline and MassTraces::intensity_profile promote every f32 with the Linux x86_64 Release build's cvtss2sd rather than with a Rust cast (update_baseline since fix round 6, whose baseline reaches the stored score_fit and score_correlation through both fitters), and avg_mz and intensity_profile follow that build's SSE instructions for every sum, product and quotient as well (cvtss2sd, addsd, mulsd, divsd with the executed operand order; libOpenMS.so 0x18f1570 and 0x18f1912), so a NaN they create or pass on carries the executed sign and payload on every host; finite results are unchanged (port/ffap-complete fix round 5: an all-zero trace's average is printed as -nan by the executed FeatureFinderAlgorithmPicked debug .plot file, ../oracle/ffap-complete-fix5, tests/feature_finder_picked_instrumentation.rs)
